scope: Cell-level review of name/number-tree source duties as used by named destinations and page labels; bounded to current source and consumer assertions.

primary_source.effective: ISO 32000-2:2020 plus Errata Collection 3 annotations in the held primary PDF

errata.effect: Strikes lexical terminology in §7.9.6 sorting prose and Table 36 Names row. The remaining operative rules specify common-prefix shorter-first order, consistent key encoding and byte-by-byte equality; no new order is introduced.
Adds 'Keys shall not be the null object' to Table 36 Names and Table 37 Nums. Writer constraint; does not specify mandatory reader rejection/recovery.
Adds 'and indices' to clarify that visible labels and fixed zero-based indices may differ.
Accepted strike/caret changes the alphabetic range example from ZZ/zz to AZ/az, implying odometer progression.
Accepted insertion adds AAA–ZZZ and AAAA–ZZZZ for each next 26, implying repeated letters. Conflicts with #432; both are retained in effective-source record, not silently reconciled.

ledger.title: Name trees
ledger.relevant_claims: Root/leaf/intermediate shape; byte string keys; exact equality/order; Limits-assisted lookup; pair enumeration; producer value/reference conventions.

ledger.title: Number trees
ledger.relevant_claims: Integer keys and ascending numeric order; Nums pairs; parallel node/Limits structure.

ledger.title: Page labels
ledger.relevant_claims: Number-tree ranges, range boundary behavior, Table 161 S/P/St and label output; #432/#593 conflict disclosed in note and ADR0601.

features.title: Root, intermediate, leaf; Kids, Names, Limits
features.source_cells: Table 36 physical 135-136 / printed 120-121. Root has exactly one of Kids/Names; a Names root is sole node. Nonroot intermediate has Kids+Limits; nonroot leaf Names+Limits. Kids are immediate-child indirect refs. Names is alternating string-key/value pairs. Limits are exact low/high descendant or leaf key bounds and forbidden on root.
features.current_code: crates/pdf-syntax/src/tree.rs::lookup/descend/admit, name_pairs, collect; public Destination::named resolves /Dests through this tree.
current_assertions: crates/pdf-syntax/src/tree.rs::a_key_is_found_through_intermediate_nodes (mechanics only; direct child dictionaries are not a valid producer fixture)
crates/pdf-syntax/src/tree.rs::a_null_key_yields_nothing_and_leaves_its_neighbours_paired (malformed-input tolerance, not a conformance rejection test)
features.verdict: The valid public test now covers a root->intermediate->leaf exact-xref structure with indirect Kids, exact Limits and both branches. The generic test's direct Kids do not establish source-validity, but no longer stand alone.
features.residuals: No requirement to reject direct Kids or malformed nodes inferred from producer-form cells. False Limits may hide a key because lookup treats present bounds as a branch gate; any recovery policy is separate from these producer duties.

features.title: String-key ordering, equality, value types and null-key erratum
features.source_cells: §7.9.6 opening bullets and prose after Table 36, physical 134-135 / printed 119-120; #214/#307 physical 135 / printed 120. Strings, not Name objects, are keys. Keys shall be byte-equal under a consistent encoding; common-prefix shorter key precedes longer. Values may be any object; stream values shall be indirect, complex dictionary/array/string values should be indirect, simple values should be direct.
features.current_code: TreeKey::Name compares string bytes; tree lookup does not interpret names as text. Name-tree writers and destination lookup use byte identity.
current_assertions: crates/pdf-model/tests/deep_name_tree_spec_audit.rs::named_destination_lookup_descends_valid_indirect_nodes_and_uses_exact_byte_keys (A/a different pages, branch keys and missing B)
crates/pdf-model/tests/trees_rectangles_audit.rs::name_tree_lookup_uses_exact_bytes_and_distinguishes_prefixes (flat exact bytes; storage sequence is sorted)
features.verdict: Valid deep public lookup now asserts byte case distinction and exact Limits. #214 leaves explicit comparator rules after removing the word lexical. #307's null-key rule is directed to producers; tolerant pair-preservation is implementation behavior, not reader conformance duty.
features.residuals: No exhaustive reader test for every allowed value type or writer-indirectness preference. No reader rejection rule follows from SHOULD directness preferences.

features.title: Kids, Nums, Limits and integer ordering
features.source_cells: Table 37 physical 137-138 / printed 122-123. Kids are indirect refs to immediate children; Nums is integer/value pairs in root or leaves; intermediate and leaf Limits are two integer extrema; integer keys are ascending numerically. #307 additionally prohibits null keys at the producer.
features.current_code: crates/pdf-syntax/src/tree.rs::TreeKey::Number, lookup, number_pairs and collect; PageLabels consumes number_pairs. Archive preservation and ParentTree consumers also use number trees.
current_assertions: crates/pdf-syntax/src/tree.rs::a_number_trees_pairs_come_back_in_order (numeric mechanics; check fixture shape before treating as source-conforming)
features.verdict: A valid public PageLabels consumer test now covers indirect multilevel number-tree enumeration with exact [0,2] and [10,10] Limits and literal boundary outputs. PageLabels sorts collected ranges itself, so this is not independent evidence for generic number-tree traversal ordering. Existing tree and archive assertions cover numeric pair ordering/writer paths.
features.residuals: Do not call the PageLabels test a generic numeric comparator oracle. Generic malformed ordering and null keys remain producer-invalid cases with no mandated reader recovery.

features.title: Page index, number-tree range, and Table 161 Type/S/P/St
features.source_cells: §12.4.2 and Table 161 physical 473-474 / printed 458-459; #73 physical 473 / printed 458; #432/#593 physical 474 / printed 459. Keys are page-index starts, tree includes index 0, ranges do not overlap, and labels increment sequentially within each range. Type optional but PageLabel if present; S optional with no default (no numeric portion when absent); P optional text prefix; St optional integer >=1, default 1.
features.current_code: crates/pdf-model/src/page_label.rs::PageLabels::read/label, Style::read, roman, letters, prefix. Consumers include navigation and accessibility. Transform split/merge/update/archive paths preserve or rebuild ranges.
features.verdict: Examples, sequential range boundary/default St, corpus first-page behavior and deep indirect tree enumeration are asserted. The current unit tests exercise absent S style parsing indirectly but no public-consumer test pins absent S and P's explicit no-numeric/empty-label behavior; a small valid fixture draft is provided.
features.residuals: The alphabetic continuation is genuinely ambiguous: accepted #432 says odometer; accepted #593 and base 'next 26' count support repeated letters. Implementation preserves repeat and ledger records disagreement. This is a source/errata conflict, not a newly observed runtime defect.

selected_adrs.reason: Bytes-vs-Name distinction for tree key identity; current exact-byte public assertions are the relevant check.
Tree traversal shape and bounded mechanics; current valid indirect deep consumer fixtures supersede older direct-child test concern.
Page-label letters decision; remains explicitly qualified by conflicting accepted #432 and #593.
Page-label range maintenance for appended pages; relevant writer path but not a new reader failure.

remaining_work: This is a bounded source-cell and assertion review, not certification of all name/number-tree consumers, tree writer shapes, or page-label display UI. No additional test is proposed for generic number lookup: valid deep name/number consumers are already covered, and PageLabels sorting limits the interpretation of its test as described.
